note: PARTIAL GT: 408x230 billboard photo. Two red Cyrillic slogan lines plus a Latin photographer watermark. Re-annotated 2026-08-01 at DETECTOR scale, which is the convention the rest of this corpus already states (cf. russian-billboard, rue-des-martyrs, quai-des-orfevres, la-bastille-1789). Glyph extents were measured by colour threshold -- red-dominant (R minus max(G,B) > 40) for the slogan, min-channel > 150 for the white watermark on its black bar -- giving [85,63,113,18], [82,85,210,19] and [297,209,106,18]. Each is then padded by 6px on every side and clamped to the frame; that single rule produces all three boxes below, and no box was copied from a detector run. The first annotation of this file used the tight glyph extents, and that was the same mistake russian-billboard and la-bastille-1789 both record having made: the recognizer needs margin around a crop, so the detector's natural boxes for these lines are 30-35px tall against a 15-18px glyph extent, and IoU-0.5 scoring against tight boxes measures the annotation rather than the detection. Measured on this asset: the pipeline reads 'В БУДУЩЕЕ' exactly at 0.928 over [80,55,126,34] and scored it a total miss at IoU 0.41. RECALL UNDER THIS FILE IS NOT COMPARABLE to recall under the previous one -- same regions, different boxes, and nothing about detection changed between them. The watermark text is also corrected: the credit line reads 'Valentina Ursu (RFE/RL)' in full (verified at 8x), and the previous entry truncated it to 'Valentina Ursu', penalising a correct read of the rest. The old note's claim that language discovery is CJK-only is stale -- PROBE_LANGSETS_EXTENDED covers Cyrillic since d830d4f, though probe_uncovered_surfaces still walks only the CJK tier. Marked partial because the lower half (Red Square crowd, black letterbox bar) was not exhaustively verified for small text. Current failure this asset pins: the slogan is read with Latin homoglyphs substituted into Cyrillic words -- 'BMЕСTЕ С РОССИЕЙ!' for 'ВМЕСТЕ С РОССИЕЙ!', where B, M and T are Latin -- because a joint (ru, en) charset has nothing constraining which script a shared letterform decodes to.
